claim: The main axis of emotion space is valence
published: PC1 26% of variance; r = 0.81 with human valence (Claude Sonnet 4.5)
ours: PC1 48% of variance; |r| = 0.94 [0.92, 0.96] with human valence (shuffled-label 95th pct 0.12); 71 emotions, 1651 stories
PC2 9% of variance; |r| = 0.06 with human arousal

claim: Emotion vectors track danger in the user's situation
published: 'afraid' rises and 'calm' falls with the Tylenol dose (Fig. 3)
ours: slope per decade of dose: afraid +4.74, calm -7.28

claim: Steering with emotion vectors shifts preferences
published: blissful steering on an option raises its Elo (+212), hostile lowers it (−303)
ours: P(choose A): baseline 0.54, +blissful on A 0.55, +hostile on A 0.54, random vector 0.53 (shifts from baseline, 95% CI over 120 pairs: blissful [-0.002, +0.010], hostile [-0.003, +0.008], random [-0.018, -0.006])
criterion: blissful > baseline > hostile, each by ≥ 0.05, with |random − baseline| < 0.05

claim: Confirmatory: emotion vectors track danger, not the size of the number
published: 'afraid' rises and 'calm' falls with the Tylenol dose (Fig. 3)
ours: slope of the afraid − calm projection per decade of dose, mean over 8 templates: Tylenol +6.52 (permutation p 0.0001), sugar +4.57; Tylenol − sugar p 0.1042
criterion: Tylenol slope > 0 with p < 0.05 and Tylenol − sugar > 0 with p < 0.05; partial if only the first (pre-stated 2026-11-28)
